Cush
kŭsh
n. (eldest son of Ham; also the land south of Egypt, rendered Ethiopia in the KJV; Hebrew Kush)
Hebrew Kush, the name of Ham's firstborn and of the territory his descendants held beyond the rivers of Egypt. The KJV usually translates the land as Ethiopia and keeps Cush for the man.

Biblical Definition

Cush is first a man and then a country. In the table of nations he stands first among the sons of Ham, father of Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabtecha — and, notoriously, of Nimrod, who “began to be a mighty one in the earth” (Gen 10:8) and built Babel. From that one line come both the tower of rebellion and the far southern nation that Scripture repeatedly holds up as the edge of the known world. Isaiah names Cush among the places from which the LORD will recover the remnant of His people the second time (Isa 11:11), setting it beside Assyria, Egypt, Elam, and Shinar in a list of the lands of dispersion. The prophets use the country as a measure of distance and of difference — can the Ethiopian change his skin? — and then overturn the measure with promise: from beyond the rivers of Ethiopia the suppliants shall bring an offering, and Ethiopia shall soon stretch out her hands unto God. The Ethiopian eunuch reading Isaiah in his chariot is that promise arriving.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) does not enter Cush; the name is fixed by the Hebrew text as Ham's eldest son and the land of his posterity.

expand to see more

The proper name is not entered in Webster's 1828 dictionary, which omits the Scripture gentilics.

CUSH. The eldest son of Ham, and the country peopled by his descendants.

ETHIOPIA, the term by which the Authorized Version usually renders the land of Cush.

The region lay south of Egypt, beyond the cataracts, and is described as beyond the rivers of Ethiopia.

From Cush descended Nimrod, the founder of Babel and the first named empire builder.

Key Scripture

Gen 10:6 — "And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan."

Gen 10:7 — "And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha: and the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan."

Gen 10:8 — "And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth."

Isa 11:11 — "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea."

Modern Corruption

Ham's line has been abused to prop a doctrine of cursed races, which the text of Genesis flatly refuses.

expand to see more

The name of Cush sits inside one of the most abused passages in Scripture. Noah's curse in Genesis 9 fell upon Canaan, not upon Ham and not upon Ham's other sons, and it was worked out in the dispossession of the Canaanite tribes before Israel. Cush is named in the very next chapter as Ham's firstborn and is never placed under that curse. Any reading that stretches the words over a whole branch of the human family is a fabrication laid on the text, and it collapses the moment the sentence is read as written. Scripture knows one blood of which God made all nations, one Adam fallen, one Christ raised.

The recovery is to follow what Scripture actually does with Cush, which is to make it the far horizon that the gospel reaches. The land beyond the rivers is named among the countries of the dispersion from which the remnant is recovered; from beyond those rivers the suppliants bring an offering; Ethiopia stretches out her hands unto God. Then Philip is sent down a desert road to one man from that country, reading the prophet, and the far horizon comes home. The line that produced Nimrod and Babel also receives, by grace, an early Gentile convert going on his way rejoicing.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Kush (H3568), Cush; Kushi (H3569), a Cushite or Ethiopian; the KJV commonly renders the land as Ethiopia.

expand to see more

Hebrew Kush (H3568) — Cush, son of Ham and the land of his seed; Genesis 10:6, Isaiah 11:11.

Hebrew Kushi (H3569) — a Cushite, Ethiopian; Jeremiah 13:23, Jeremiah 38:7.

Hebrew Nimrod (H5248) — Nimrod, son of Cush, builder of Babel; Genesis 10:8-10.

Greek Aithiops (G128) — an Ethiopian; Acts 8:27.

The Authorized Version usually renders the land Ethiopia and reserves Cush for the man and a few place references.

Usage

"“And Cush begat Nimrod” — the line from which Babel came."

"“From Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar” — the lands of the second recovery."

"“The sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim” — first in the Hamite table of nations."
